primary_source: Lin Chen and Dragomir Z. Djokovic, Properties and construction of extreme bipartite states having positive partial transpose, arXiv:1203.1364v1, https://arxiv.org/html/1203.1364v1, Theorems 37 and 38. This is a public source read AFTER the f88edb60 source-screen proposal and AFTER the earlier unrestricted rank-cut packet; source reading is not an independent proof of its results.
theorem37_exact_scope: For M,N>2, an MxN PPT entangled state of rank N+1 is reducible if and only if its range contains a product vector, and equivalently is a Bob-direct sum with a pure product state. Consequently, an extreme PPT entangled state of rank N+1 has a completely entangled range. This already supplies the proposed rank-(n+1) CES conclusion for the state without assuming SN>=3. Applying it to the partial transpose when that is extreme and has rank N+1 supplies the analogous partial-transpose conclusion. It is NOT a new research contribution; novelty of any more general fiber inequality remains unclear.
theorem38_exact_scope: For M,N>3, every MxN PPT entangled state of rank N+1 is reducible with a pure product direct summand, so there are no such extreme states. In particular no extreme full-local 4x4 PPT entangled state has rank five. Since partial transpose is an affine automorphism of the PPT set, preserves local ranks and preserves entanglement, the same excludes partial-transpose rank five. Thus, conditional on the public theorem, the full-local 4x4 extreme branch of the unrestricted target has both ranks at least six, stronger than the rank-at-least-five statement of packet 6681aab4. The local-(3,4) branch is not eliminated: the paper explicitly constructs 3x4 extreme PPT states of rank five.
